landmarks.name: Mausoleum Hadriani
sourceGeometryTitles: OSM Location: Mauseoleum of Hadrian
landmarks.chronologyDescription: Mausoleum Hadriani (now Castel Sant'Angelo) located on the right bank of the Tiber River was an imperial mausoleum built by Hadrian between 134 and 139 CE. It continued as a tomb for subsequent emperors through to Caracalla, who died in 217 CE. By 401 the tomb had become a fortress with Honorius incorporating it into the line of the Aurelianic walls. During Alaric's sacking of Rome in 410 the mausoleum was looted and the ash urns dispersed. Procopius describes the destruction of the tomb's bronze statuary in 537. By the fourteenth century, the mausoleum had become a papal fortress. At one point, a fortified corridor known as Passetto di Borgo connected the fortress to St. Peter's Basilica.
landmarks.notes: Footprint is central drum. AD 320 tomb had square plinth and no medieval castle bastions, papal apartments or angel statue.

landmarks.name: Colossus Neronis
sourceGeometryTitles: OSM location of pedestal of colossus of Nero
landmarks.chronologyDescription: The "Colossus Neronis" or "Colossal Statue of Nero" was a monumental bronze statue of the first-century CE emperor reportedly created by Zenodorus. The statue was originally an element of the sprawling Domus Aurea of Nero but the monument endured long after Nero's reign. The statue's original position likely marked the summit of the Velian Hill. The Flavians refashioned the statue to resemble Sol and Hadrian relocated the statue nearer the Flavian amphitheater as part of the work to create the Temple of Venus and Roma.

bridges.reconstruction: Ancient elevation schematic; endpoints from modern bridge axis except Aemilius extrapolated from fragment.

island.notes: Modern footprint clipped to omit the upstream alluvial spit. Ancient shoreline is explicitly schematic.

aqueductModel.alignmentStatus: The first mapped fragment is retained from the existing dataset. The continuation follows the documented Porta Maggiore–Caelian–Palatine relationship as a schematic visual route, not a surveyed centerline.
aqueductModel.phase320: The Neronian branch and its Domitianic Palatine extension pre-date AD 320; the arcade was restored under Septimius Severus.

water.branchNotes: Approximate north channel traced around the source island shoreline and mapped bridge axes; not an ancient measured riverbank.

terrainModel.notice: No vertical exaggeration. All heights are approximate model levels, not a complete surveyed reconstruction of AD 320.

sources.title: ISPRA・SIGEA, Geodiversità urbana Roma (2023), pp. 5–12
sources.use: Volcanic plateau remnants, incised valleys, Velia and the Capitoline–Quirinal connection. Model polygons are our approximation.

sources.title: Moscatelli et al., Integrated geological and geophysical investigations to characterize the anthropic layer of the Palatine hill and Roman Forum (2013)
sources.use: Hill-top elevations around 49 m in the surveyed excavation area; terraces, foundation structures and steep flanks. Not a city-wide ancient DEM.

sources.title: コロッセオ考古学公園：パラティーノ
sources.use: Imperial palace precinct on the Palatine.

sources.title: Digital Augustan Rome：Palatium
sources.use: Broad summit plateau; especially steep south-west and north-west flanks; low saddle and only gradual ascent toward the Velia on the north-east. Augustan topography is used for landform constraints only, not to back-date buildings to AD 320.

sources.title: コロッセオ考古学公園：スタディウム・パラティーノ
sources.use: The palace stadium measures about 161 × 48 m and lies about 10 m below the main palace level. Its late inner oval is not projected back to AD 320.

sources.title: コロッセオ考古学公園：Kronos e Kairos（セウェルス朝区画）
sources.use: Severan arcades form an artificial south-eastern terrace about 23 m high, with 17 arches and an approximately 3,500 m² upper surface; the Maxentian works of 306–312 connected the upper Circus area.

sources.title: コロッセオ考古学公園：ドムス・ティベリアーナ
sources.use: The approximately four-hectare palace occupies the north-western slope; imperial architecture and substructures are distinct from the natural hill profile.

sources.title: Mancini et al., Stratigraphy of the Palatine Hill (2018)
sources.use: The hill is a roughly 25 ha flat-topped landform near 50 m a.s.l., separated by the Velabrum, Murcia and Labicana valleys. The 25 ha whole hill is not treated as the summit plateau area.

sources.title: Rome Transformed：Arcus Neroniani
sources.use: The Aqua Claudia branch ran from Porta Maggiore to the Temple of Divus Claudius on a double brick arcade and received a major Severan restoration. Used for identity, phase and the Porta Maggiore–Caelian relationship; the model continuation is explicitly schematic.

sources.title: アッピア街道考古学公園：Aqua Claudia / Anio Novus
sources.use: Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus reached Porta Maggiore on arches, with secondary branches serving the Caelian and Palatine. Used as the network context for the modeled Arcus Neroniani.
